definitions.explanation: A symbol in musical notation that represents the pitch and duration of a sound. Also refers to the sound itself that the symbol represents.

examples.japanese: {音符|おんぷ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
{音符|おんぷ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}くて→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: There are many notes and it's difficult.

examples.japanese: ⟦{楽譜|がくふ}→楽譜：06987_gakufu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{音符|おんぷ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦ずつ→ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{読|よ}んでいく→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I read the musical notes on the sheet music one by one.

examples.japanese: {四分|しぶん}{音符|おんぷ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{八分|はちぶん}{音符|おんぷ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦リズム→リズム：04746_rizumu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}した→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧。
examples.english: I practiced the rhythm of quarter notes and eighth notes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}どもたち→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{音符|おんぷ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{書|か}き{方|かた}→書き方：13054_kakikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}っている→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: The children are learning how to write musical notes.

notes:
TYPES OF NOTES:
Japanese names note values by the fraction they occupy of a whole note, so they are transparent once the pattern is clear — unlike the English names, which a learner has to memorise separately.
- {全|ぜん}{音符|おんぷ}: whole note (semibreve)
- {二分|にぶん}{音符|おんぷ}: half note (minim)
- {四分|しぶん}{音符|おんぷ}: quarter note (crotchet)
- {八分|はちぶん}{音符|おんぷ}: eighth note (quaver)
- {十六分|じゅうろくぶん}{音符|おんぷ}: sixteenth note (semiquaver)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {音符|おんぷ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to read notes
- {音符|おんぷ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write notes
- {音符|おんぷ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to be unable to read music

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- ⟦{休符|きゅうふ}→休符：07538_kyuufu⟧: a rest — the silence counterpart, named on the same fractional pattern
- ⟦{楽譜|がくふ}→楽譜：06987_gakufu⟧: the score the notes are written on
- ⟦{音程|おんてい}→音程：07109_ontei⟧: pitch or interval — how high a note is, as opposed to how long
